question: When we choose an AI tool, how do we know we are paying for real results and not just extra features?
reflection: Careful testing on our own tasks, rather than trusting habit or reputation, helps every team spend wisely and learn faster.

sources.subject: Understanding the "harness tax" behind coding agents

one_line: A new study suggests the software wrapped around an AI model can change its cost several times over with little change in results.

top_stories.title: The wrapper can double the bill
top_stories.what: Researchers tested seven models in three coding-agent wrappers and report that the same model on the same task cost up to five times more in some wrappers, with similar success rates.
top_stories.why: Any team buying AI agents should compare cost per successful task on its own work, not rely on the vendor's default setup.

top_stories.title: Simple setups hold their own
top_stories.what: A minimal wrapper with only four basic tools reportedly matched or beat feature-rich ones on value, and models did not always do best in their own vendor's wrapper.
top_stories.why: Starting simple and adding features only when they fix a real problem is a sound rule for public-sector AI pilots too.

saudi_lens.text: No direct Saudi link today, though the lesson on testing cost per result applies to any government agency procuring AI agents.

idea.title: AI pilot cost-per-result check
idea.pitch: Offer a short audit that compares two or three AI tool setups on a client's real tasks and reports cost per successful outcome.
idea.first_step: Pick ten routine tasks from one project and define what a successful result looks like for each.

idea_kids.title: Same job, different tools challenge
idea_kids.pitch: Children build the same paper tower with different sets of tools and materials, then count what each set cost and how tall it got.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare three tool kits with simple prices and a score sheet for height and cost.

terms.definition: The software around a model that gives it instructions, tools and memory so it can act as an agent.
What it costs to get one task done successfully, counting failed attempts and retries.

concepts.summary: The choice of model and the wrapper around it should be tested together.
Smarter setup choices can cut AI spending without losing quality.
